headline_marked: [[Trezor confirms data breach]] of email provider, exposing 347,000 crypto owners to scams
headline: Trezor confirms data breach of email provider, exposing 347,000 crypto owners to scams
summary: A cyberattack on Trezor's email provider, Brevo, led to 347,000 phishing emails being sent to customers, attempting to steal wallet backup passwords and crypto funds.
details: Hardware crypto wallet maker Trezor is warning customers for the second time in as many months about a data breach at one of its third-party providers. A cyberattack on Brevo, a marketing tech company Trezor uses for newsletters, exposed customer data.

This breach allowed hackers to send approximately 347,000 phishing emails to Trezor customers. These emails contained malicious links designed to download an app that prompts victims for their wallet backup passwords.

One of the phishing email subject lines observed was "Critical Security Alert: STM32 Entropy Vulnerability." If a hacker obtains a wallet password, they can irreversibly steal funds from the victim's public blockchain.

Brevo stated that hackers accessed 138 of their accounts due to a flaw where access was "not properly scoped" and "wrongly granted" to all reachable organizations. This highlights a common security risk involving third-party vendor compromises.

Trezor confirmed that its own products, wallets, and account systems were not directly affected by this incident. However, this is the second breach for Trezor in recent weeks, following an August incident with shipping partner ShipMonk.

The ShipMonk breach exposed names, phone numbers, email addresses, and postal addresses of at least 81,000 Trezor hardware wallet buyers. Such data breaches can put crypto owners at risk of targeted violence, including "wrench attacks" to extract passwords.

In the aftermath of the ShipMonk breach, some customers received physical letters with QR codes leading to fake pages designed to steal crypto wallet passwords. Trezor is now reevaluating its vendor relationships and has warned customers to expect further phishing attempts.

Customers are advised to remain vigilant against any suspicious communications. Always verify the source of emails and links, and never enter sensitive information like wallet backup passwords unless absolutely certain of authenticity.

headline_marked: [[Neuro Engine cuts AI coding token waste]] by up to 96%, slashing pay-as-you-go bills
headline: Neuro Engine cuts AI coding token waste by up to 96%, slashing pay-as-you-go bills
summary: This new MCP server analyzes code skeletons, allowing AI to emit compact 20-token change blueprints instead of rewriting entire files, reducing monthly costs from $300-600 to $30-50.
details: Neuro Engine dramatically reduces AI coding costs by analyzing code skeletons and only requiring compact 20-token change blueprints. This eliminates the need for AI models to rewrite entire 500-line files for minor changes, saving up to 96% on token usage.

This efficiency translates to significant cost savings, cutting monthly pay-as-you-go bills from $300-$600 down to approximately $30-$50. It also extends the utility of fast requests on services like Cursor and Claude Pro, allowing 5x-10x more tasks before hitting caps.

The system prevents context bloat, which often saturates AI models' context caches and triggers rolling message limits after just a few hours of continuous work. By minimizing context, Neuro Engine enables continuous coding sessions for a full 10-hour day without throttling.

Neuro Engine supports 16 programming languages, including Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, C, C++, C#, Java, Kotlin, PHP, Ruby, SQL, HTML, CSS, Vue, and Svelte. It also offers critical security features, scrubbing API keys, JWTs, and private data locally before AI models see the context.

It includes safeguards against common coding errors, instantly reverting git workspace changes if code fails syntax checks or linter validation. This prevents corrupted files and ensures clean application boots even with multi-file prompts and auto-wired imports.

The official stable release is set for Tuesday, September 15, 2026, with canary builds available earlier for founders. Initial access is strictly limited to 1,000 developer licenses, offered as a permanent binary access with zero recurring subscriptions.

Users can track their savings with `neuro-engine stats`, which displays exact tokens bypassed and dollar savings directly in the terminal. A 100% refund is offered if active coding sessions fail to save tokens or reduce spend after 30 days, upon telemetry report submission.
